name: Tranquility Base
description: First crewed landing, southwestern Mare Tranquillitatis. Equatorial near side: Earth always high in the sky, ~14 days of sunlight then ~14 days of night.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Ocean of Storms
description: Pinpoint landing next to Surveyor 3 in Oceanus Procellarum.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Fra Mauro
description: Fra Mauro highlands, ejecta of the Imbrium basin.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Hadley–Apennine
description: Between the Apennine mountains and Hadley Rille; first Lunar Roving Vehicle.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Descartes Highlands
description: Only Apollo landing in the central lunar highlands.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Taurus–Littrow
description: Valley on the southeastern rim of Mare Serenitatis; last crewed landing to date.
coordinateNote: Lunar Module position from LRO images (Wagner et al. 2017), Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame, DE421.

name: Odysseus (Malapert A region)
description: First CLPS landing and southernmost landing at the time. Low Sun all lunar day; Earth only a few degrees above the horizon.
coordinateNote: Resting position measured by LRO / LROC.

name: Athena (Mons Mouton)
description: Landed on the Mons Mouton plateau ~160 km from the south pole, inside a 20 m crater; carried the PRIME-1 ice-mining demo.

name: Blue Ghost (Mare Crisium)
description: First fully successful commercial lunar landing, near Mons Latreille in eastern Mare Crisium.

name: Vikram — Shiv Shakti Point
description: First landing in the south polar region (~600 km from the pole), between Manzinus C and Simpelius N craters.

name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
description: Japan's precision-landing demonstrator, on the slope near Shioli crater (near side).

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán)
description: First landing on the far side, in Von Kármán crater (South Pole–Aitken basin). Earth is never visible: relay satellite required.

name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin)
description: First far-side sample return, southern Apollo basin. No direct line of sight to Earth.
coordinateNote: LROC-computed position −41.6385°, 206.0148°E (±30 m), expressed here as 153.9852°W.

name: Shackleton crater (centre)
description: 21 km crater almost on the south pole. Its floor is permanently shadowed and holds cold traps for water ice; its rim and the connecting ridge are among the best-lit places on the Moon.
coordinateNote: Feature centre from the IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (LOLA-based).

name: Artemis III candidate regions (9)
description: Peak near Cabeus B, Haworth, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton Plateau, Mons Mouton, Nobile Rim 1, Nobile Rim 2, de Gerlache Rim 2, Slater Plain. NASA published the regions on a map only (≈15×15 km each).
